rows.whatWasActuallyWrong:
THE ROW, not the election — and the two were told apart by three independent tests rather than by reading FIX105 or VF11.

(1) WHAT THE FORM ASKS. The pinned source CN-10557 (c1dd37b5e27bd76ea2330b07f51847c420d359db8f10c0576682e6558d09c5f7) was rastered at 300 dpi and page 19 item (d) was read by eye and with pdftotext -layout. Item (d) is ONE sworn compound sentence, not a checkbox with optional decoration: "On (date) __ I pled/was found guilty/adjudicated delinquent of the charges of (name of offense(s)) __, in violation of N.J.S.A. (statute(s)) __ and sentenced to (final sentence) __ by the (name of Court) __ Court. I completed (jail/prison/incarceration time) __ on (date) __; probation on (date) __ and I paid the fine(s) on (date) __." Marking the box beside `d.` swears that whole sentence. The nine cells the row group names are the nine blanks of that sentence; the two continuation lines (guiltyOff2, guiltyFinal2) are correctly excluded as optional.

(2) WHAT THE PLATFORM HOLDS. The build`s fixture fact sets (factsCanonical / factsBoundary in scripts/build-census-v1-nj_arrest_no_conviction-set.mjs, lines 220-258) were read directly. Of the nine cells the platform holds three: guiltyDt (matter.conviction_date), guiltyOff1 (matter.charge), guiltyCrt (matter.court). Six are unmapped: guiltyStatute, guiltyFinal1, guiltyTimeType, guiltyDocCmpltDt, guiltyProbDt, guiltyFineDt.

(3) WHETHER THE MISSING SIX COULD BE SUPPLIED — the test that decides whether this is a build defect or a legal-input gap. Each of the six was checked against the route`s OWN committed intake, in both places it is recorded: legal-design-track-registry.json generationRequirements and legal-design-intake/NJ.memo.json participantInputs. THREE ARE COLLECTED and are merely absent from the fixture persona: guiltyStatute is collected by indMatterDetails/dpoMatterDetails/ordMatterDetails ("For each matter: ... the offence and statute ..."), and guiltyDocCmpltDt and guiltyProbDt are collected by indSentenceCompletion/dpoSentenceCompletion/ordSentenceCompletion ("When did you finish probation or parole, or get released from custody, on each matter?"). THREE ARE NOT COLLECTED BY ANY QUESTION ON ANY OF THE THREE TRACKS: guiltyFinal1, the FINAL SENTENCE IMPOSED — no intake question on any track asks what sentence was imposed; guiltyTimeType, the JAIL/PRISON/INCARCERATION TERM — an AcroForm dropdown whose options were read first-hand from the pinned binary with pdf-lib and are exactly ["  ","jail time","prison time","incarceration time"], with NO none/not-applicable option, so a participant who served no custodial term has no honest value and the platform holds no fact saying which of the three applies; and guiltyFineDt, the DATE FINES WERE PAID — indFinancialAssessment/dpoFinancialAssessment/ordFinancialAssessment ask only WHETHER every fine was paid, never when, although the same tracks` waitingPeriods run from "payment of any court-ordered financial assessment", which is a real internal inconsistency in the committed record and is reported below rather than resolved here.

(4) WHETHER ANY OTHER CONTROL COULD STATE THE ROUTE INSTEAD. Every non-text field on the kit was enumerated from the family`s own field census: 19 checkboxes and 14 dropdowns. On the participant`s petition the only route-shaped elections are the disposition boxes a/b/c/d (pages 18-19), the two compelling-circumstances boxes on page 22 (seek5yrs, seek34degree — both conditional and both requiring an attorney-authored narrative the registry classifies as "not template output"), and seekJuvNever on the Verification page 24. seekJuvNever was examined closely because its printed text DOES name a statute — "I am seeking expungement of a conviction ... pursuant to N.J.S.A. 2C:52-2, and I have never been granted an expungement, sealing or similar relief regarding a criminal conviction, by any state or federal court." It is not a lawful substitute: it names 2C:52-2 only, so it is wrong on its face for nj_disorderly_persons (2C:52-3) and nj_ordinance (2C:52-4); and it is a COMPOUND oath whose second limb swears to a prior-expungement fact the fixture does not hold (indPriorExpungement is collected but is not in the fixture persona). Marking it would be the same defect FIX105 removed, in a worse place. There is no other control on this kit by which these petitions can state their statute.

CONCLUSION. The election is not the defect. The election is correctly withheld, exactly as FIX105 built it and VF11 ruled: the row beneath it cannot be completed, and a marked box over nine empty cells is a sworn assertion of a conviction the paragraph declines to identify. The defect is the row. The row cannot be made completable by a build lane, because three of its nine cells are facts NO committed intake question on any of these three tracks collects, and inventing fixture values for them would manufacture a capability the product does not have and put a fabricated sentence and custodial term into a sworn petition. That is a legal-design/intake gap, and closing it is a legal-input decision, not a build change. This lane therefore printed NO mark and reports the families as BLOCKED_LEGAL_INPUT on ROUTE_OPTIONS.

The alternative the assignment allowed — stop declaring one rendered — was not taken, because the route`s own committed record states the counting rule in full and a required component that the repository can answer should be answered rather than downgraded.
componentSetDisposition.whatItSays: A new section `## How the offence count works on this route`. It opens by stating in bold that the packet does NOT count the participant`s offences and decides no eligibility, and that the SBI record is what produces the count and nobody has read it. It then quotes the track registry`s own `mechanism` string WHOLE as the held counting rule, and pulls out its three operative points in plain words: the cap of five counted across disorderly persons and petty disorderly persons offences in any combination; that the same-day route and the interdependent-or-closely-related route carry no numeric cap at all, so a record over five may still qualify; and that any crime conviction moves the record off this route onto N.J.S.A. 2C:52-2. It then quotes the track`s own held openLegalQuestion warning that the Judiciary self-help page`s published "up to three disorderly persons offenses" figure describes the 2C:52-2 route and not this one, and names the held legal-design correction "Correct the disorderly persons cap from four to five". It closes with the track`s own dpoOffenceCount intake question verbatim and the three held stop conditions that bound counting.
componentSetDisposition.everySentenceCarried: Every quoted passage is read out of data/record-clearing/legal-design-track-registry.json at build time and asserted present there; nothing states a legal rule this repository does not already hold, and nothing states a count for any participant.

The section now states that no held source establishes an objection period, that none should be inferred from the packet`s silence, names the Criminal Division office in the county of filing as the place to ask, and notes that "Prosecutor objection." is a held self-help stop on this route.
